subject: Request: Clarify blended-availability calculation after routing vendor incident
messages:
From: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@everscale.com>
To: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: support@everscale.com
Date: Tue, 05 Jan 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Severe impact Jan 4-5 — routing vendor CloudTransit path fail; request for recalculation and credit

Rishi —

Thanks for taking the call yesterday. As we discussed, Everscale observed a partial availability loss across our US-West clients between 2027-01-04 22:35:00 UTC and 2027-01-05 02:10:00 UTC. Our telemetry shows ~18% of requests experienced 5xx errors or timeouts during that window; the traffic map pins the root cause to CloudTransit’s routing fabric in us-west-2.

Important context: we were in an automated maintenance window on 2027-01-04 21:50:00–22:10:00 UTC (minor rolling kernel updates applied to our fleet). Based on Everscale’s internal SLO math, the larger outage period overlaps the maintenance window but extends well beyond it while routes were flapping. We believe the net availability degradation should not be excluded in full due to the maintenance window because the majority of customer impact occurred after the maintenance end.

Request: please provide Redwood’s calculation showing how you attribute the degraded minutes across (a) our service, (b) CloudTransit routing tier, and (c) any maintenance exclusion. We’re asking for an adjustment to the uptime ledger to reflect shared responsibility and a proportional credit.

Attached: Everscale probe summary and sample request traces (probe_timeline.pdf).

Appreciate a clear breakdown so we can reconcile with procurement for our renewal.

—Lena Ortiz
CTO, Everscale Technologies
From: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 05 Jan 2027 11:04:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Severe impact Jan 4-5 — routing vendor CloudTransit path fail; request for recalculation and credit

Team —

Looping you in. Customer (Everscale) is pressing for a reworked apportionment after CloudTransit’s path instability. Key asks: full calculation, logs that show when our ingress/backend served traffic normally vs when routing failed, and a suggested credit split.

Questions I want answered before we respond to Lena:
- Ben: can you confirm our probe/ingress traces for the time window and show whether our origin RX/TX had errors or whether failures were upstream (CloudTransit)?
- Kimberly: legal/ops — what precedent do we have for overlapping customer-maintenance windows and third-party outages? Do we exclude the whole overlap or only the portion that aligns to our maintenance?

Let’s keep this tight — the renewal negotiation starts next week and this will factor into their credit ask. I’ll draft a response to Lena once we have numbers.

Thanks,
Rishi
Head of Sales — Enterprise
Redwood Inference
From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 06 Jan 2027 08:23:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Severe impact Jan 4-5 — routing vendor CloudTransit path fail; request for recalculation and credit

Rishi —

Quick technical summary and attached ledger: see uptime_ledger.csv for minute-by-minute flags. Findings: 
- Our edge fleet in us-west showed normal health checks and low error rates from 2027-01-04 21:40:00 UTC through 22:10:00 UTC (the customer’s maintenance window). No application-level 5xx spikes on our ingress during that exact maintenance interval.
- Starting at 2027-01-04 22:35:00 UTC, we observed a rise in TLS handshake failures and route timeouts correlated with CloudTransit NOC alerts. The failures persisted in bursts until 2027-01-05 02:10:00 UTC. During that period our upstream service logs show high retry rates, but origin instances remained healthy and serving when reachable.
- Probe coverage: Everscale’s probes show elevated errors beginning ~22:38 UTC, which aligns with our CloudTransit-facing telemetry. We mark minutes in three buckets: SERVICE (our causality), THIRD_PARTY (CloudTransit), and TRANSITION_OVERLAP (minutes where both maintenance and third-party errors are present). The CSV has columns: minute, flag.

Recommendation for proportional credit: allocate 60% of the degraded minutes to THIRD_PARTY, 30% to TRANSITION_OVERLAP, and 10% to SERVICE. For TRANSITION_OVERLAP minutes we propose applying only a 50% weight toward eligible credit since part of the window intersects a scheduled maintenance block initiated by the customer. That yields an effective creditable fraction of (0.6 + 0.3*0.5 + 0.1) = 0.85 of the degraded minutes.

If legal wants to contest the TRANSITION_OVERLAP weighting, we can present raw minute flags and let Procurement negotiate the split.

Attachments: uptime_ledger.csv (minute flags), probe_correlation_notes.txt (log pointers).

—Ben Carter
Senior Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Severe impact Jan 4-5 — routing vendor CloudTransit path fail; request for recalculation and credit

Lena —

Thanks for the patience while we pulled the minute-level ledger together. Attached is Redwood’s minute-by-minute ledger (uptime_ledger.csv) and a short probe-correlation summary (probe_timeline.pdf) that mirrors Ben’s notes. Summary below and next steps: 

Summary of findings (high level)
- Root cause: CloudTransit routing instability that caused intermittent route timeouts starting ~2027-01-04 22:35:00 UTC and lasting to ~2027-01-05 02:10:00 UTC.
- Maintenance overlap: Everscale’s rolling maintenance concluded at 2027-01-04 22:10:00 UTC. The majority of impacted minutes occur after that end time. There is a short transition window (22:35–22:40 UTC) when both effects are visible in traces.
- Redwood’s apportionment proposal: we attribute 60% of impacted minutes to CloudTransit, 10% to Redwood service (retry/backpressure effects we observed upstream), and 30% to the transition/overlap. For the overlap minutes we apply a 50% exclusion weight (per our standard overlap policy) which yields an aggregate creditable fraction of ~0.85 of degraded minutes.

Proposed next steps
1) We’ll share the raw minute CSV (attached) and a redlines-friendly summary so your procurement/legal can apply any contractual precedent.
2) I’ve opened a ticket with CloudTransit and copied their NOC to request their post-incident analysis and any capacity-metrics we can use to finalize a shared credit.
3) If you prefer an alternative split for the overlap weighting, let us know; we’ll recalculate and present the adjusted ledger.

We want to resolve this before your renewal discussions. If helpful, we can schedule a 30-minute working session with Ben and Kimberly to walk the minute flags.

—Rishi
Head of Sales — Enterprise
Redwood Inference

Attachments: uptime_ledger.csv, probe_timeline.pdf
